# Invariants (E)

<!-- generated by scripts/verify_docs.py --write-nav; do not hand-edit -->

> Code is the source of truth. This file is a map; when it and the code disagree, the code wins.

Every invariant is defined in exactly one file and referenced by id elsewhere.

The index is sharded by family letter: see also [`doctrine/invariants.md`](invariants.md), [`doctrine/invariants-c-d.md`](invariants-c-d.md), [`doctrine/invariants-f-m.md`](invariants-f-m.md), [`doctrine/invariants-n-pk.md`](invariants-n-pk.md), [`doctrine/invariants-pl-pq.md`](invariants-pl-pq.md), [`doctrine/invariants-pr-r.md`](invariants-pr-r.md), [`doctrine/invariants-s.md`](invariants-s.md), [`doctrine/invariants-t-z.md`](invariants-t-z.md).

| Id | Statement | Defined in |
|---|---|---|
| `INV-ENG-001` | A terminal transition has exactly one winner, and only the winner performs the finalization side effects. | [`architecture/engagement-finalization.md`](../architecture/engagement-finalization.md) |
| `INV-ENG-002` | A strict terminal transition never leaves the persisted and in-memory records disagreeing; on a write failure it restores the prior state and raises. | [`architecture/engagement-finalization.md`](../architecture/engagement-finalization.md) |
| `INV-ENG-003` | A successful completion requested through the completion tool is refused while an operator message to the engagement is admitted, or written and not yet taken up, or an inbound reservation is held, when the driver exposes its inbound state. | [`architecture/engagement-completion-gate.md`](../architecture/engagement-completion-gate.md) |
| `INV-ENG-004` | An agent reached through delegation cannot delegate onward. | [`architecture/delegation.md`](../architecture/delegation.md) |
| `INV-ENG-006` | Accepting a delegate's display name never widens the delegation ACL. | [`architecture/delegation.md`](../architecture/delegation.md) |
| `INV-ENG-007` | Every `<delegates>` block Casa builds names delegates as the ACL then resolves them. | [`architecture/delegation.md`](../architecture/delegation.md) |
| `INV-ENG-008` | Engagements created from agent context never exceed a fixed global live count, and refusal is side-effect-free. | [`architecture/delegation.md`](../architecture/delegation.md) |
| `INV-ENG-009` | Every write into an `in_casa` job's session — the brief, an operator's message, a nudge, a continue or restart line — is admitted by the registry immediately before the client call that hands it over, with no suspension point in between: a record found idle is `active` by then, and a terminal record is never written to. It does not fence the hand-off itself: a terminal transition landing once a write has begun cannot revoke it, and stopping a running session stays `driver.cancel`'s job. A refused write is never reported as delivered and never told twice. | [`architecture/engagement-turn-admission.md`](../architecture/engagement-turn-admission.md) |
| `INV-ENG-010` | Once the terminal transition is won, the funnel's tail — driver teardown, the completion notification and the finalized log — survives cancellation of the task that ran the funnel, and its payloads carry the record values frozen at the flip. | [`architecture/engagement-finalization.md`](../architecture/engagement-finalization.md) |
| `INV-ENG-018` | An engagement outcome committed by the finalization funnel carries, in the same durable write as its terminal status, the obligation to tell the party that asked for the work — except the completed end of a quiet scheduled job run nobody interacted with, which is told to no one and arms nothing, a decision the transition makes under its lock from the record's quiet stamp (INV-BGJOB-025, INV-BGJOB-015). That obligation is cleared only by the delivery acknowledgement of the notice that carries it — the notice's narration reaching the transport, or that narration turn ending in a clean chosen silence as INV-JOB-010 defines it, while a turn that ends with no text and no sentinel stays owed — never by the bus accepting the message and never by another record's acknowledgement; a record still carrying it is exempt from terminal-retention expiry, so the obligation outlives the process. Casa's boot owner replays every record that owed one when this process loaded its records and still owes it when the replay reaches it — never one this process armed, which it told live and which, if that notice is never delivered, the next boot replays — addressed from that record's own persisted origin and reporting the FACT of the outcome, never a retained answer the record does not hold; startup awaits that owner unguarded, once the channels and the resident loops are running. A replayed notice says so: it carries one replay statement after its header — an earlier outcome, reached before a Casa restart, whose announcement was never confirmed as delivered — with the time the record was committed terminal, or says that time is unknown; a missing or unusable recorded time never stops the notice from becoming a prompt and never makes a tombstone write fail, a recorded time that is not a finite number never ages the record out, and a notice sent live is never so marked. A rolled-back transition owes nothing, a row written before the field existed owes nothing, and no other terminal writer arms it by default: the two that do — the cancellation owner's launch-death report, which tells the engager over the bus, and the inline named-fault abort, whose returned envelope is the telling and whose return schedules the acknowledgement for a transition it won — opt in explicitly (INV-ENG-021). | [`architecture/engagement-terminal-telling.md`](../architecture/engagement-terminal-telling.md) |
| `INV-ENG-021` | A job launch answers `pending` to the call that launched it once the job's session is open and its brief is queued; the job's first turn never runs inside the engager's turn, and cancelling the tool call after it returned does not touch the session. A launch that ends before that answer is told to the engager exactly once — by its returned envelope (a named fault, or `launch_cancelled` when a stop latched while its session opened), acknowledged on return, or, when the launcher itself was cancelled, live over the one engagement-outcome envelope with the obligation armed in the terminal write. Telling ownership is never inferred from the record: a compensating owner that loses the terminal race tells nobody, however armed the record is; an inline arm acknowledges on return only a transition it won, and hands its telling to its own abort only when the launcher was cancelled before returning the envelope. A cancellation whose terminal write did not persist leaves the record live and tells the engager under its own non-terminal kind, which the consumer never narrates as a failure. The graceful stop drains the launch ledger, then the reporters, their acknowledgements and tellings, the named-fault aborts and the cancelled launchers' owners together to joint quiescence, and once it has marked those drains complete neither a cancelled launcher's compensation nor a named-fault abort mints anything; each is logged. | [`architecture/engagement-launch-detach.md`](../architecture/engagement-launch-detach.md) |
| `INV-ENG-024` | A delegated run that the wall-clock ceiling ends, or that is cancelled from outside, leaves no proven descendant of its CLI running once the runner has raised — a process a plugin server started after the session began included — and a process it cannot confirm gone is logged at ERROR with the role and the pids. | [`architecture/delegation.md`](../architecture/delegation.md) |
| `INV-ENG-025` | `hand_off` runs only inside a specialist's own delegated or desk run, to a loaded specialist that is not already in the request's chain, and never past three hand-offs after the resident the chain started from; every refusal happens before any run, permit or record exists. | [`architecture/specialist-handoff.md`](../architecture/specialist-handoff.md) |
| `INV-ENG-026` | The time a delegated run spends waiting on its own hand-offs does not count against its wall-clock ceiling. | [`architecture/specialist-handoff.md`](../architecture/specialist-handoff.md) |
| `INV-ENG-027` | Once an `in_casa` engagement's terminal status is on disk and `TRANSCRIPT_RETENTION_DAYS` have passed since its `completed_at`, a pass run at scheduler start and every six hours deletes its CLI transcripts — a plugin job's whole per-engagement project folder, or, for a specialist or executor, the session the record names in that record's own project folder — each only where the run-confirmation gate passes, and a plugin job's working folder `/data/engagements/<id>` at once, and selects nothing else. A pass that cannot import the SDK's folder lookup deletes no transcript. | [`architecture/engagement-transcript-reaping.md`](../architecture/engagement-transcript-reaping.md) |
| `INV-ENG-028` | An ephemeral delegation runs under the session id Casa chooses for that launch, or for a continuation the one its binding keeps, registered in `transcript_runs` before its request is captured and before its client starts; the run is confirmed only once its request's and its answer's captures are durable or the live rules capture nothing; its transcript is deleted only by the delegated retention pass or a wipe — that one session, in its own project folder, once the run is confirmed and `TRANSCRIPT_RETENTION_DAYS` have passed since it ended — and an unconfirmed run's transcript never by retention; the utility one-shots (the tier classifier, `query_engager`'s synthesis, run admission's reading) persist no transcript at all. | [`architecture/engagement-transcript-reaping.md`](../architecture/engagement-transcript-reaping.md) |
| `INV-ENG-029` | A message to a job — a reply into it, a tapped answer, an approval's continuation — that the job never reads draws exactly one bounded notice attempt, made by the seam when the job did not accept it and otherwise by the job's message journal once the job ended without reading it, never by a caller of the seam; a message from the operator's direct chat is told there in reply to their message or the tapped card, worded from the record's settled status, and no terminal outcome lists such messages. | [`architecture/engagement-inbound-disclosure.md`](../architecture/engagement-inbound-disclosure.md) |
| `INV-ENG-030` | A launch that ends after its record exists and before it answered — its launcher cancelled, or Casa's stop latched while its session opened — is reported by one owner, the launch-death reporter, which asks the registry one strict terminal question and lets its three outcomes decide: a durable win writes one line in the job's log, tears the driver down under a bound and settles the job's message journal; a lost race performs no side effect; a rolled-back persist leaves the record live with the client retired. The path writes only `error`, never `completed`. | [`architecture/engagement-launch-detach.md`](../architecture/engagement-launch-detach.md) |
| `INV-ENG-031` | A named launch-failure arm settles its job only on the strength of a terminal transition this call both won and durably persisted; a transition another writer won, and one whose persist rolled back leaving the record live, leave the record and the job to their owner; on all three outcomes the arm answers its caller with its own named fault and posts nothing. | [`architecture/engagement-failure-and-restart.md`](../architecture/engagement-failure-and-restart.md) |
| `INV-EV-001` | Only an operator-consented, currently-reconciled route ever dispatches an event wake, and every unrouted pair's queued emissions are deleted every authoritative pass. | [`architecture/plugin-events.md`](../architecture/plugin-events.md) |
| `INV-EV-002` | Fold mints at most one generation and one delivery ladder per idle pass, and no queued emission is ever lost to it. | [`architecture/plugin-events.md`](../architecture/plugin-events.md) |
| `INV-EV-003` | A subscription's consent binds subscriber, subscriber artifact id, emitter, event, declaration digest and sorted delivery targets as one identity, and any change to them unroutes the pair without resurrecting it later. | [`architecture/plugin-events.md`](../architecture/plugin-events.md) |
| `INV-EV-004` | Every delivery record eventually reaches `done` carrying exactly one durable outcome, redelivered on a fixed six-slot ladder until receipt or budget exhaustion. | [`architecture/plugin-events.md`](../architecture/plugin-events.md) |
| `INV-EV-005` | An ack token, the emission envelope, and the mint payload never reach a log line, a health surface, an operator notice, or a tool reply beyond naming the acked subscriber, and an ack mutates a record only on a live token match at that record's current generation. | [`architecture/plugin-events.md`](../architecture/plugin-events.md) |
| `INV-EV-006` | An event-dispatched turn is marked as an internal wake by a context key no external ingress can set, and an interactive input request inside that turn is mechanically refused. | [`architecture/plugin-events.md`](../architecture/plugin-events.md) |
| `INV-EV-007` | An operator note the worker attempts while the Telegram channel is not ready, before the channels have finished starting, is logged at INFO without a traceback, and an owed exhaustion or removal note stays owed; every other failed note keeps an ERROR with its traceback. | [`architecture/plugin-events.md`](../architecture/plugin-events.md) |
| `INV-EVAL-001` | The tester registry is empty; no evaluator is registered or invoked. | [`architecture/eval-framework.md`](../architecture/eval-framework.md) |
| `INV-EVAL-002` | Bank selection for any live-memory check comes from the caller; the code does not confine it. | [`architecture/eval-framework.md`](../architecture/eval-framework.md) |
